subject: Can Excel sort more than 6 columns into DISTANCE hierarchy?

messages.author: 397224dbeee02a09
messages.subject: Can Excel sort more than 6 columns into DISTANCE hierarchy?
parts:
Has anyone figured out a way to use Excel to sort more than 6 columns of
data into the proper hierarchy for DISTANCE, and, more importantly, can
you explain your method? Or, must one manually separate data by some
level, sort the individual levels, then re-stack the data for import into
DISTANCE? Is there a program you prefer for this task (e.g. SAS,
ACCESS)?

Thanks for your time!

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Can Excel sort more than 6 columns into DISTANCE hierarchy?
parts:
Hi David,

I may be missing something, but in Excel:
- click on the top left cell (the one above row 1 and to the left of
column A) to select all cells in the worksheet
- from the menu bar, choose Data | Sort...
- select to "Sort by" the column corresponding to stratum label, and
"Then by" the column corresponding to sample label
- click OK
- Save as a text file and import this into Distance

I just tried this with a >6 column worksheet and it worked fine, using
Excel 2003.

If this is not what you meant, please contact me off the list - we can
work out what you did mean and how to achieve it, and then post the
answer to the list.

- Len Thomas
